status: Storyboard and production plan; generated video not included

storyboard_generation_prompt: Create a premium photorealistic CINEMATIC STORYBOARD SHEET for an architectural glazing website hero film called THE THRESHOLD. This is concept visualization, not a real contractor project. Use the attached entrance photograph as visual reference for the single architectural world: white precast/concrete columns, slim graphite aluminum mullions, perfectly clear glass, stainless vertical pull handles, pale terrazzo floor, California trees outside, warm interior light. Preserve these materials and plausible geometry throughout. No people, no logos, no client names, no flying glass, no sci-fi holograms, no construction magic. Format a tall portrait art-direction board with TWO COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS of exactly EIGHT separate cinematic landscape 16:9 frames. Crisp white gutters and white paper background. At top restrained large graphite sans-serif title THE THRESHOLD and small subtitle 16 SECOND HERO FILM / EIGHT SHOTS. Each frame has only a small clean 01-08 number beneath it, no explanatory text. Film grade: bright white, graphite and soft steel-blue reflections, realistic warm sunlight. Architecture is photographed like a high-end lens commercial, not a CGI render. Strong filmic lighting without orange teal grading, stars or anamorphic flare gimmicks. Shot 01 extreme macro looking along the polished EDGE of a stationary glass pane against almost black graphite, a single fine white vertical reflection forming a luminous line; striking material abstraction. Shot 02 very close oblique view of the same glass surface, reflected pale blue sky and a tree, dark mullion at the side, a narrow warm light reflection. Shot 03 sharp macro joint of vertical and horizontal graphite aluminum framing with realistic gasket detail, diagonal composition but perfectly straight framing. Shot 04 low macro on the bottom seal and threshold beside the glass entrance, a hard stripe of natural sunlight across pale stone, crisp detail. Shot 05 three-quarter near view of the same graphite glass entrance door opening normally on hinges toward the outside, long stainless pull handle, inviting warm lobby beyond; no visible person. Shot 06 low camera at the threshold looking inward through the open doorway, same central white columns, horizontal floor joints leading into luminous interior; strong forward-perspective momentum. Shot 07 a restrained wide interior shot of the same white commercial lobby and graphite glass office fronts, a beautiful sharply defined shaft of afternoon light on the terrazzo; calm final spatial reveal. Shot 08 wide exterior three-quarter final view of that SAME glass entrance and white precast building at blue hour, warm light behind glass and quiet pale steel-blue sky, understated dramatic architecture, center opening clearly visible with straight columns and matching doors. Make the visual contrast between intimate material details and the final spatial reveal extraordinary. Every frame must be beautiful on its own and remain physically coherent. This board is reference for generating separate video shots in local models, not a video itself.
